nodes.label: Ultra-wide-like perspective
nodes.description: The widest ordinary lens family: it swallows a huge amount of the room and stretches whatever is nearest the camera, so hands, feet and edges of the frame look exaggerated. Focal length is INFERRED from those perspective cues, never read from the file, so the label always says 'like'.
examples: a whole cramped bedroom visible from one corner
a skateboarder's board looming huge in the foreground
nodes.prompt_fragment: ultra-wide-angle-like perspective

nodes.label: 14mm-like ultra-wide perspective
nodes.description: An extremely wide view in which straight lines still stay straight, so whole interiors, tall buildings or huge skies fit in one frame while near objects balloon towards the viewer. The millimetre figure is an inference from that stretch, not a measurement.
examples: an entire small kitchen captured from the doorway
a skyscraper leaning away overhead
nodes.prompt_fragment: 14mm-like ultra-wide perspective

nodes.label: Fisheye-like perspective
nodes.description: An extreme wide view that deliberately bends straight lines outward, so horizons curve and the middle of the picture bulges towards you. Unlike other wide lenses this bending is the point and is never corrected.
examples: a skateboarder filmed from ground level with a curved horizon
a whole room bowing around a face pushed close to the camera
nodes.prompt_fragment: fisheye-like ultra-wide perspective with curved lines

nodes.label: Wide-angle-like perspective
nodes.description: A lens family that takes in noticeably more of the surroundings than the human eye finds natural, pushing the background away and giving near objects a gentle forward stretch. Focal length is INFERRED from those cues and is always rendered as an approximation.
examples: a person in a doorway with the whole street visible behind them
a table setting with the entire dining room around it
nodes.prompt_fragment: wide-angle-like perspective

nodes.label: 24mm-like wide perspective
nodes.description: A distinctly wide view that keeps a whole figure and a generous slice of the place in one frame, with visible stretch at the edges but no cartoon-like bending. The number is an estimate drawn from that perspective, not a claim about the camera.
examples: a full-length figure with a wide street behind them
a handheld vlog frame holding both face and room
nodes.prompt_fragment: 24mm-like wide-angle perspective

nodes.label: 28mm-like perspective
nodes.description: A mildly wide view, close to what most phone cameras produce: a little more of the room than the eye expects, with only slight stretch near the edges.
examples: a casual phone snapshot of friends at a table
a street portrait that still shows the shopfront behind
nodes.prompt_fragment: 28mm-like perspective

nodes.label: 35mm-like perspective
nodes.description: The classic reportage view: slightly wider than the eye, so a person and the place they are standing in both read clearly without obvious distortion. This is inferred from how much context sits around the subject, never asserted as a fact about the camera.
examples: a documentary frame of a person walking a busy pavement
an environmental portrait in a workshop
nodes.prompt_fragment: 35mm-like perspective

nodes.label: Normal-lens-like perspective
nodes.description: The neutral middle of the range, where near and far look about as far apart as they do to the naked eye and nothing is visibly stretched or squashed. Because there are no distortion cues to read, this class is the most cautious inference of all.
examples: a straightforward portrait with an unremarkable background
a still life that looks the way it looked in the room
nodes.prompt_fragment: normal-lens-like natural perspective

nodes.label: 50mm-like perspective
nodes.description: The everyday standard view: a face is rendered honestly, the background sits at a believable distance, and nothing about the geometry draws attention to itself. The millimetre figure is a best guess read from the picture.
examples: a half-length portrait with an ordinary room behind
a plate of food seen the way a diner would see it
nodes.prompt_fragment: 50mm-like natural perspective

nodes.label: Telephoto-like perspective
nodes.description: A long lens family that appears to pull distant things closer and stacks the background right up behind the subject, flattening the sense of depth. Focal length is INFERRED from that flattening and from how quickly the background falls out of focus.
examples: a runner picked out of a crowd with the buildings squashed behind
a portrait where the far treeline sits directly behind the head
nodes.prompt_fragment: telephoto-like compressed perspective

nodes.label: 85mm-like perspective
nodes.description: The classic portrait view: features are rendered flatteringly without stretch, and the background softens and closes in behind the head. Read from the gentle compression and background blur rather than from any camera data.
examples: a head-and-shoulders portrait with a creamy background
a fashion shot where the wall behind sits soft and close
nodes.prompt_fragment: 85mm-like short-telephoto perspective

nodes.label: 135mm-like perspective
nodes.description: A longer portrait view that isolates the subject hard: the background is strongly flattened and dissolves quickly, and the camera is clearly standing well back.
examples: a face isolated against a wash of distant city lights
a runway shot taken from the end of the catwalk
nodes.prompt_fragment: 135mm-like telephoto perspective

nodes.label: 200mm-like long-telephoto perspective
nodes.description: A very long view shot from a long way off, so distant layers pile up almost on top of each other and the subject appears cut out of a soft wall of background. Sports and wildlife pictures look like this.
examples: a footballer sharp against a melted blur of stadium crowd
a bird on a branch with the whole forest reduced to soft colour
nodes.prompt_fragment: 200mm-like long-telephoto perspective with strongly compressed depth

nodes.label: Macro-like close focus
nodes.description: A lens able to focus so close that a small thing fills the whole frame at near life size, revealing texture the eye cannot normally resolve, with only a paper-thin sliver of the picture in focus.
examples: the weave of a fabric filling the frame
a water droplet on a petal, everything else soft
nodes.prompt_fragment: macro-like extreme close focus

nodes.label: Tilt-shift-like plane of focus
nodes.description: A lens whose focus runs as a narrow band across the picture instead of a flat slab, so a real street can look like a tiny model with only one stripe sharp. It can also straighten converging building lines.
examples: a city block from above looking like a toy set
a tall facade photographed with vertical lines kept parallel
nodes.prompt_fragment: tilt-shift-like selective plane of focus

nodes.label: Anamorphic-like rendering
nodes.description: The wide cinema lens character: out-of-focus highlights stretch into ovals rather than circles, the edges of the frame smear slightly, and bright lights streak sideways. It describes the rendering, not the focal length, so it can sit alongside any of the focal classes.
examples: a night interior with oval highlight blobs behind the actor
a widescreen frame with a horizontal streak across a headlamp
nodes.prompt_fragment: anamorphic-like widescreen rendering with oval bokeh

nodes.label: Shallow depth of field
nodes.description: Only a thin slice of the picture is sharp and everything in front of and behind it melts away, which is what pulls a subject cleanly off its background.
examples: sharp eyes with the ears already going soft
a coffee cup crisp while the cafe behind dissolves
nodes.prompt_fragment: shallow depth of field, the background falling away into soft blur like a fast lens wide open
nodes.negative_fragment: no shallow depth of field, keep the background legible

nodes.label: Deep focus
nodes.description: Everything from the nearest object to the far distance stays sharp at once, so the viewer can read foreground and background as equally important.
examples: a landscape where both the near rocks and the mountains are crisp
an interior where a face and the far doorway are both readable
nodes.prompt_fragment: deep focus, foreground and distance both sharp like a stopped-down lens

nodes.label: Heavy bokeh
nodes.description: The out-of-focus areas are not merely blurred but decorative: bright points behind the subject bloom into soft rounded discs of light.
examples: city lights behind a face turning into glowing circles
fairy lights melting into soft globes
nodes.prompt_fragment: heavy bokeh, background highlights blooming into soft rounded discs, reminiscent of a fast portrait lens

nodes.label: Soft focus
nodes.description: The whole picture keeps its shapes but loses its hard edges, with bright areas glowing gently outwards, the way an old portrait or a diffusion filter looks.
examples: a window-lit portrait with a gentle halo around the highlights
a hazy, romantic close-up with no crisp edges
nodes.prompt_fragment: soft-focus rendering, highlights glowing gently, reminiscent of a diffusion filter
nodes.negative_fragment: no soft-focus diffusion, keep edges crisp

nodes.label: Focus pull
nodes.description: During the shot the sharp area travels from one thing to another, for example from a hand in the foreground to the face behind it, moving the viewer's attention without moving the camera. It only exists in moving footage.
examples: focus drifting from the raindrops on the glass to the face beyond
sharpness handing over from the speaker to the listener
nodes.prompt_fragment: a focus pull shifting sharpness from one plane to another, rack-focus-like
nodes.negative_fragment: no focus pull, hold focus throughout

nodes.label: Compressed perspective
nodes.description: Distant layers appear stacked almost on top of one another, so a far-off building or a crowd looks much closer to the subject than it really is. This is the main visual cue that a long lens was used.
examples: a sunset sun looking enormous directly behind a walking figure
a row of parked cars squashed into a single flat band
nodes.prompt_fragment: compressed perspective stacking the background close behind the subject, like a long lens

nodes.label: Barrel distortion
nodes.description: Straight lines such as door frames and horizons bow gently outwards and objects near the edge of the frame look stretched, a side effect of very wide lenses.
examples: a doorway subtly bowing at the edge of the picture
a face near the frame edge looking slightly pulled sideways
nodes.prompt_fragment: slight barrel distortion bowing straight lines outward, like a wide-angle lens
nodes.negative_fragment: no barrel distortion, keep straight lines straight

nodes.label: Vignetting
nodes.description: The corners of the picture sit noticeably darker than the middle, which quietly pushes the viewer's eye towards the centre.
examples: a portrait whose corners fall gently into shadow
a film still with darkened frame edges
nodes.prompt_fragment: gentle corner vignetting, like a fast lens shot wide open
nodes.negative_fragment: no vignetting, even brightness to the corners

nodes.label: Lens flare
nodes.description: A bright light source just inside or outside the frame scatters inside the lens, throwing streaks, coloured blobs or a milky haze across the picture.
examples: a low sun throwing a streak across a face
a street lamp casting a coloured ghost across the frame
nodes.prompt_fragment: lens flare streaking from a bright light source, similar to an uncoated vintage lens

nodes.label: Anamorphic flare
nodes.description: The signature horizontal blue-white streak that shoots sideways out of every bright light, the most recognisable trait of wide cinema lenses.
examples: a headlamp drawing a long blue line across a night frame
a practical bulb streaking sideways behind an actor
nodes.prompt_fragment: horizontal blue streak flares from bright lights, anamorphic-like
